realProviderResults.reason: Not run: the deployment hold and paused manual testing (28 Oct). A real run would spend from the shared money and search limits (/day, 0/month; 10/100 public searches), which stay unchanged. When allowed, run each question once and report each run on its own, not as a benchmark.

whatThisProves: What the code refuses or keeps for each case, whatever the model proposes. It does not measure how often a real model proposes the wrong reply, or the quality of real search results.
knownLimits: Conflicting official pages: only amounts are compared, only for the same capitalised subject, and only across pages that were actually read. A disagreement about a rule, date or eligibility in words is not detected. Two amounts with different scopes (per year vs a two-year card) are treated as a disagreement, so the reply must state both.
Emirates: only the listed hosts are tied to an emirate (others count as federal), and a conversation naming two emirates sets none, so no emirate check runs then.
England-only gov.uk pages are recognised only when the page text names England and no other nation.
A sentence that names the page’s place ("In Dubai, …", "In England, …") is allowed for someone elsewhere: it says whose rules they are.
Scripted model: these cases show what the code refuses or keeps, not how often a real model proposes the wrong reply.
